title: Generic fields and normalization components of a finite etale cover
statement:
Let $X$ be a normal integral Noetherian scheme, with function field $F$, and let $p:Y\to X$ be finite etale [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sc-function-field, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and normal means every local ring is an integrally closed domain. There is a finite set $I$ and a disjoint union $Y=\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i$ into nonempty open and closed integral normal subschemes. Each $Y_i\to X$ is finite etale and surjective. Put $F_i=k(Y_i)$. There are compatible identifications
$$Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F\cong\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}F_i,$$
where each $F_i/F$ is finite separable; moreover $Y_i$ is canonically the normalization of $X$ in $F_i$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Thus every field factor of the generic finite etale algebra is the function field of exactly one $Y_i$, and its normalization over $X$ is finite etale. The empty cover corresponds to $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0BQL, lemma-finite-etale-covering-normal-unramified, statement and first proof paragraph (finite decomposition into integral normal components, generic points dominate); generic finite etale field factors as in Tag 02GL, morphisms-lemma-etale-over-field.

proof.text: First $Y$ is Noetherian. Indeed, over any affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, finiteness gives $p^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite list of module generators also generates $B$ as an $A$-algebra; and the single affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a finite affine cover of the inverse image. Thus $p$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the given Noetherian $X$.

source.place: Tag 0BQL, lemma-finite-etale-covering-normal-unramified, first proof paragraph; Noetherian specialization justified by Morphisms Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] to the etale map $Y\to X$, using step 1 and normal integrality of $X$. This gives a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed normal integral subschemes $Y_i$. Write $I$ for the finite indexing set. Each $Y_i$ is nonempty because an integral scheme is nonempty [def-pc-integral-scheme]. If $Y$ is empty use the empty family. Conversely a nonempty summand cannot occur in an empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 0BQL, first proof paragraph, normality and disjoint integral components; Properties Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-clopen-restriction] to each nonempty clopen $Y_i\subseteq Y$. The base $X$ is irreducible because it is integral. Thus each $p_i:Y_i\to X$ is finite etale and surjective.

source.place: Tags 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite), 01WK (lemma-composition-finite), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), and 03WT (lemma-etale-open): restriction to a clopen source subset, followed by the open-and-closed image argument over an irreducible target.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-integral-finite-etale-generic-field] to $p_i$ between the integral schemes $Y_i$ and $X$. It gives the finite separable extension $F_i/F$ and the canonical component generic-fibre isomorphism, with both projections.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2), with Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); affine generic fibre and localization calculation in the proof of the returned item, step 5.

proof.text: Each open subscheme $Y_i$ is locally Noetherian, since $Y$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is normal integral by step 2, and $F_i/F$ is finite by step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normal-cover-normalization] to $p_i$. Its affine integral-closure equalities give the canonical normalization isomorphism inducing the identity on $F_i$. This normalization is finite etale by step 3.

source.place: Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), applied to the generic-point map and a finite normal integral cover; Properties Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections) and Algebra Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral). Affine integral-closure argument of returned steps 6--7.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] to $Y=\coprod_iY_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$. With the component identifications of step 4 this gives the required compatible $F$-isomorphism $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F\cong\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}F_i$. Equivalently its algebra is $\prod_iF_i$. The primitive nonzero idempotents of a finite product of fields are exactly the coordinate idempotents: an idempotent in a field is $0$ or $1$, and one with two nonzero coordinates splits into two orthogonal nonzero idempotents. Hence every field factor, understood as a factor indexed by its primitive idempotent, comes from exactly one component $Y_i$; distinct isomorphic field factors are still distinct factors. Step 5 identifies its normalization with that $Y_i$. All assertions for the empty cover hold with $I=\varnothing$, the empty fibre and the zero generic algebra.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_normal_generic_components {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X] (hX : ∀ x : X, IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (p : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite p] [Etale p] : ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → Y.Opens) (hI : ∀ i, IsIntegral (U i).toScheme) (A : ∀ i, Algebra X.functionField (U i).toScheme.functionField), (∀ i, IsClosed (U i : Set Y)) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (U i) (U j)) ∧ (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ (n = 0 ↔ IsEmpty Y) ∧ (∀ i, (∀ y : (U i).toScheme, IsIntegrallyClosed ((U i).toScheme.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧ IsFinite ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ Etale ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ Surjective ((U i).ι ≫ p) ∧ FiniteDimensional X.functionField (U i).toScheme.functionField ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable X.functionField (U i).toScheme.functionField ∧ ∃! e : (U i).toScheme ≅ X.normalizationIn (U i).toScheme.functionField, e.hom ≫ X.fromNormalizationIn (U i).toScheme.functionField = (U i).ι ≫ p ∧ (U i).toScheme.fromSpecFunctionField ≫ e.hom = (X.fromSpecOfAlgebraFunctionField (U i).toScheme.functionField).toNormalization) ∧ ∃ e : (∐ fun i : Fin n ↦ Spec (U i).toScheme.functionField) ≅ pullback p X.fromSpecFunctionField, ∀ i, Sigma.ι (fun j : Fin n ↦ Spec (U j).toScheme.functionField) i ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.fst p X.fromSpecFunctionField = (U i).toScheme.fromSpecFunctionField ≫ (U i).ι ∧ Sigma.ι (fun j : Fin n ↦ Spec (U j).toScheme.functionField) i ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd p X.fromSpecFunctionField = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap X.functionField (U i).toScheme.functionField))
